  "entries": [
    {
      "name_han": "太上三皇宝斋神仙上录经",
      "logic_thesis": "This text proves that immortality is not a private mental achievement but a juridical-liturgical status granted when pure zhai, correct offerings, and the Sanhuang register cohere. Personal refinement alone is insufficient; only sustained abstinence, lamp-smoke, and petition that clear seven-generation debt can rewrite the celestial ledger and admit the adept to the immortal roster.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Three Sovereigns hold the prenatal register that names life, death, and rank.
Premise 2: Multigenerational sin and impurity block the register from opening to the living.
Inference 1: Therefore only rigorous zhai (silence, timed meals, pure water, incense) can sever contamination and make petition audible.
Inference 2: When lamps and fragrant beads transmit intent, heavenly officers reverse black-book entries and fix the immortal name.
Conclusion: Long life and spirit-summoning power are consequences of register correction, not of technique without liturgy.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Treat chart-clearing as zhai before reading BaZi: fix intention, reduce sensory noise, then open the pillars.
2. Sequence work as debt → purity → petition: first name ancestral and personal blockages, then refine qi, then act.
3. Use timed “lamp” discipline (fixed watches of quiet focus) to mark when intention is clean enough to decide.
4. Do not attempt spirit-calling or fate-override operations until three sustained cycles of purity have held.
5. Measure success by lighter body-mind and freer timing, not by dramatic visions.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 三皇内秘文, which argues from cosmogony and seal-command, this text argues from ritual procedure and register law. Unlike later Jingming ethics texts, it does not moralize social virtue first; it moralizes purity and petition as the only legitimate path into the Sanhuang bureaucracy."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "太清金阙玉华仙书八极神章三皇内秘文",
      "logic_thesis": "This text proves that all spirits, disasters, and remedies are effects of one generative process: True-One → yuanqi → differentiation into heaven, earth, humans, gods, and deviant classes. Command over ghosts and disease is therefore legitimate only when the operator re-aligns with that same True-One hierarchy, not when he merely stacks stronger spells.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Before images, True-One already moves; yuanqi self-transforms into clear, turbid, harmonious, and deviant forms.
Premise 2: Eight Extremes, Five Peaks, and ghost-types are handles of that one body of qi, not rival cosmologies.
Inference 1: Evil is misaligned residue of the same root, so it answers to names and seals that restore order.
Inference 2: Therefore talisman and summoning work only when the operator’s moral-cosmic station matches the chapter’s hierarchy.
Conclusion: Mastery of the Sanhuang secret chapters is re-participation in cosmogony, which then authorizes exorcism and protection.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Map BaZi ten gods and six relations onto “classes of qi” (supportive, deviant, pure, turbid) rather than as mere labels.
2. Before remedial rituals, state the root principle (True-One / yuanqi) so technique is not freestanding magic.
3. Rank remedies: first correct self-station and timing, then address external “ghost” or disaster patterns.
4. Use directional/Eight Extremes thinking for spatial luck: treat place as a handle of the same qi body.
5. Reject techniques that claim power without re-centering the operator in the generative hierarchy.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from 思印气诀法 by supplying ontology before method; seals here are secondary to cosmology. It differs from pure Zhuangzi commentaries by treating hierarchy and command as real, not as illusions to dissolve—why the text can authorize active demonology rather than only contemplative freedom."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "思印气诀法",
      "logic_thesis": "This text proves that a seal’s efficacy is not material inscription alone but the temporary identity of mind-image, directed qi, and ritual seal. When tooth-clicking, mudra, paced steps, inhaled qi, and visualization fuse, the seal becomes a portable center of command that can bind landscape, illness, and disorder.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Spirits and places respond to concentrated intention embodied as form.
Premise 2: Qi follows breath and attention; seals store and project that form.
Inference 1: Therefore the operator must first assemble inner court (teeth, mudra, Yu steps, color-coded officers).
Inference 2: Blowing qi into the seal charges the form; stamping or sealing then transfers that charge to a target domain.
Conclusion: Control of mountains, seas, epidemics, or thieves is the extension of a completed mind-qi-seal circuit, not of ink alone.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Before any BaZi remedy or space-clearing, complete a short assembly: settle breath, set intention, form a clear “seal” image of the desired order.
2. Use paced movement and timed exhalation to move qi into a concrete symbol (hand, talisman, or written name).
3. Apply the charged form only to one domain at a time (room, body, conflict) to avoid diffuse intention.
4. After stamping/sealing, withdraw qi and store the form; do not leave residual excitement.
5. Test efficacy by environmental shift (calmer place, fewer disruptions), not by emotional hype.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 三皇宝斋, which proves through multi-day zhai and celestial ledger, this text proves through a compact operational circuit. Unlike 中黄八柱经, which builds an internal architecture of virtue and orifices, 思印气诀法 externalizes the same mind-qi unity into a tool that acts on the outer world."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "南華真經註疏",
      "logic_thesis": "Cheng Xuanying’s double-mystery (chongxuan) reading proves that liberation is the successive emptying of both attachment and attachment-to-emptiness. Guo Xiang’s “each thing is self-so” is not final; the adept must also forget the very stance of self-so, so that neither being nor non-being remains as a grip.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Fixed is/ought dualisms generate suffering and false mastery.
Premise 2: Guo Xiang dissolves artificial standards into natural allotment (ziran, duxua).
Inference 1: Yet holding “allotment” as doctrine reinstalls a subtle self.
Inference 2: Therefore one must negate both affirmation and negation (twofold mystery).
Conclusion: True free-and-easy wandering is not settling into nature as an idea, but the unobstructed functioning after both poles drop.",
      "logic_practice": "1. When a BaZi pattern feels fatal, first drop moral panic, then drop the pride of “accepting fate.”
2. Practice two-step release: name the attachment, then name the attachment to being free of it.
3. Use chart reading as diagnosis of current conditions, not as an identity the self must defend.
4. In meditation, alternate “rest in what is” with “do not rest even in resting” for short cycles.
5. Measure progress by reduced need to win interpretive fights about destiny.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from Wang Pang’s 新傳, which retools Zhuangzi for political-moral usefulness, by treating usefulness itself as a trap to empty. It differs from Lin Xiyi’s 口義, which clarifies plain sense for readers, by pushing beyond sense into a method of successive apophasis."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "南華真經新傳",
      "logic_thesis": "Wang Pang proves that Zhuangzi’s free wandering is not social withdrawal but the inner basis of correct public order: only a mind that has loosened private compulsion can respond to affairs without distortion. The text argues that Daoist freedom and Confucian responsibility are one continuum when the heart is no longer hijacked by fixed names.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Political and personal disorder arise from stiff names and private desire.
Premise 2: Zhuangzi’s transformation and equalization loosen those grips.
Inference 1: A loosened mind can then take up roles without being owned by them.
Inference 2: Therefore commentary must translate parable into principles of self-governance and statecraft.
Conclusion: The “new transmission” is Zhuangzi re-proved as practical wisdom for ordering self and realm, not as aesthetic escapism.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Read day/luck pillars as roles you inhabit, not as essences you are.
2. Before major decisions, ask: is this response from loosened awareness or from a name I am defending?
3. Train “useful uselessness”: keep capacity without forcing every hour into achievement.
4. In conflict charts, equalize viewpoints first, then choose the action that least reinstalls compulsion.
5. Use cultivation to improve public-facing clarity (speech, timing), not only private calm.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike Cheng Xuanying’s double mystery, which empties both poles, Wang Pang stops at a usable equilibrium that serves ethics and politics. Unlike 無能子, which weaponizes naturalness against hierarchy, 新傳 rehabilitated hierarchy by purifying the mind that must still act within it."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "南華真經口義",
      "logic_thesis": "Lin Xiyi proves that Zhuangzi’s difficulty is largely pedagogical: when parable, humor, and “absurd” images are restored to spoken sense, the argument about transforming life becomes teachable without esoteric monopoly. Clarity of ordinary language is itself a method of equalizing access to the Dao.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Obscure classical glosses recreate the very scholastic ego Zhuangzi mocks.
Premise 2: Oral paraphrase recovers narrative intent and human situation.
Inference 1: Therefore correct understanding is tested by whether a listener can apply it today.
Inference 2: Application without jargon dissolves false profundity.
Conclusion: “Mouth-meaning” is not vulgarization but a proof that the Dao operates in plain life when speech stops performing status.",
      "logic_practice": "1. After any BaZi analysis, restate the whole chart in one plain sentence a non-specialist could use.
2. Drop ornamental jargon in cultivation notes; keep only verbs of practice.
3. Teach transformation with stories of daily pressure (work, family), not only with classical tags.
4. Use humor and self-undercutting to break reading-as-status.
5. Verify insight by behavioral change within one week, not by elegant formulation.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from 義海纂微 by refusing encyclopedic plurality in favor of one lucid reading path. It differs from 循本, which seeks philological “original intent,” by prioritizing living intelligibility over archaeological purity—why Lin’s text became a gateway rather than a scholarly fortress."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "南華真經義海纂微",
      "logic_thesis": "Chu Boxiu proves that no single commentator owns Zhuangzi; truth emerges by setting many lineages side by side until shared structure and productive differences appear. Anthology is an epistemic method: the “sea of meanings” disciplines both sectarian capture and private whim.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Guo, Cheng, Song Confucians, and Daoist readers each catch partial angles.
Premise 2: Isolated reading mistakes a partial angle for the whole.
Inference 1: Collecting and arranging them reveals recurring logic (equalization, transformation, free wandering).
Inference 2: Divergence then becomes diagnostic of method, not merely error.
Conclusion: Understanding is a comparative operation across a tradition, not submission to one master voice.",
      "logic_practice": "1. For hard BaZi questions, deliberately consult three incompatible models, then extract only the overlapping constraints.
2. Keep a comparative notebook: same passage / chart feature, multiple readings, one residual certainty.
3. Treat disagreement as information about method bias (moral, empty, political, philological).
4. Refuse early closure when only one school flatters your preference.
5. Synthesize practice rules only after patterns recur across sources.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 口義’s single plain path, 義海纂微 multiplies paths to prevent monopoly. Unlike 循本, which rejects Chan-tinged and freestyle notes to recover “the root,” Chu’s work preserves the archive so that “the root” can be checked against history rather than asserted."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "南華真經章句音義",
      "logic_thesis": "Chen Jingyuan proves that sound, graph, and chapter division are not pedantry but the first filters of thought: wrong pronunciation and false segmentation generate metaphysical ghosts. Philology is thus a spiritual hygiene that returns the text’s movement before doctrine is built.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Meaning rides on correct wording, rhythm, and unit of argument.
Premise 2: Later metaphysics often rests on corrupt or forced readings.
Inference 1: Therefore chapter-and-sentence work and sound-meaning notes must precede lofty claims.
Inference 2: Where Yijing and correlative patterns genuinely help structure, they must still answer to the restored text.
Conclusion: Authentic free wandering begins with textual fidelity that prevents self-projected Dao.",
      "logic_practice": "1. In BaZi, define every technical term before interpreting (what “cai” means operationally this month).
2. Re-segment life narratives: wrong “chapter breaks” create false destiny stories.
3. Prefer small, text-true rules over grand symbolic systems that ignore data.
4. When using Five-Phase or Yijing overlays, demand a textual or observational warrant.
5. Audit your own notes for words that sound deep but do no diagnostic work.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from Cheng’s mystical double-emptying by starting below metaphysics, at the letter. It differs from Wang Pang’s moral-political rewrite by refusing to skip the text’s grain; Chen’s “why” is that corrupt sound-sense is already a form of self-assertion."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "南華真經循本",
      "logic_thesis": "Luo Miandao proves that later Zhuangzi industries—pure talk, forced Yijing, and Chan overlays—lose the book’s own spine (for him, often “transformation” as continuous thread). Returning to the root is a critical method: cut secondary cleverness until the text’s native argument reappears.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Commentarial fashion multiplies meanings that serve schools, not Zhuangzi.
Premise 2: A text has internal recurrence and narrative logic that can discipline reading.
Inference 1: Tracking that internal thread (“follow the root”) exposes alien grafts.
Inference 2: What cannot be justified by the text’s own movement is set aside.
Conclusion: Liberation teaching must be reclaimed from hybrid display and restored to Zhuangzi’s self-consistent path.",
      "logic_practice": "1. For any cultivation claim, ask: what single thread in my practice does this serve? Drop ornaments.
2. In chart work, pick one structural key (e.g., useful god, day-master balance) and follow it end-to-end.
3. Reject methods that only add prestige metaphors without changing decisions.
4. Periodically return to primary experiences (breath, timing, consequence) to reset theory.
5. Prefer fewer consistent rules over a collage of impressive schools.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 義海纂微’s generous archive, 循本 is exclusionary by design: plurality is the disease. Unlike 口義’s accessibility project, Luo’s project is authenticity policing—why his “why” is anti-syncretic where Lin’s is anti-elitist."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "沖虛至德真經解",
      "logic_thesis": "Jiang Yu’s Liezi commentary proves that stories of dreams, skill, fate, and the infinite are engines for releasing the will’s claim to mastery. Reading Liezi correctly means converting marvel into a discipline of yielding: destiny is not denied, but the anxious self that fights destiny is dissolved.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Liezi multiplies limit-cases (dream/waking, finite/infinite, effort/fate).
Premise 2: These cases break ordinary agency without preaching nihilism.
Inference 1: Commentary must show how each tale loosens a specific grip (control, fame, cleverness).
Inference 2: The freed person then acts with skill like the butcher or boatman—without forcing.
Conclusion: Chongxu (“pouring emptiness”) is proven as practical non-resistance that still allows exquisite function.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Use hard luck periods as dream/waking training: notice which “self” is panicking.
2. Practice skill-without-forcing in one craft (speech, writing, body work) as Liezi’s craftsmen do.
3. When BaZi shows constraint, shift from “how do I overturn” to “where is non-resistance intelligent.”
4. Alternate contemplation of vast scale (time, heaven) with next small action.
5. Drop debates that only restore the will’s sense of control.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike Zhuangzi’s more rhetorical equalization, Liezi (as Jiang reads it) often proves through narrative shock and fatalism-tempered skill. Unlike 四解, which layers four authorities, this single-author 解 seeks a unified Guo-like philosophical voice rather than a chorus."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "沖虛至德真經四解",
      "logic_thesis": "The four-layer Liezi (Zhang Zhan, Lu Chongxuan, Huizong, Fan Zhixu) proves that the same parable supports successive altitudes of reading—from metaphysical emptiness to cultivated practice to imperial instruction—without collapsing into one slogan. Multi-commentary is a ladder: each rung answers a different failure mode of the reader.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: A single gloss cannot serve novices, adepts, and rulers equally.
Premise 2: Liezi’s tales are polyvalent by design.
Inference 1: Stacking historically distinct exegeses exposes complementary functions of one story.
Inference 2: The reader learns to choose the layer that corrects their present disease (doubt, rigidity, ambition, despair).
Conclusion: “Four explanations” demonstrate that truth is one process of emptying and trusting process, taught through calibrated voices.",
      "logic_practice": "1. For one life problem, write four responses: empty view, practice view, ethical view, strategic view; keep only what reduces friction.
2. Use Zhang-style ontology when anxious about meaning; use practice layers when lazy or diffuse.
3. In BaZi teaching, match explanation depth to the querent’s actual bottleneck.
4. Do not force imperial/political readings onto private grief, or private quietism onto public duty.
5. Revisit the same classic seasonally; different layers will “light up.”",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from Jiang Yu’s single philosophical 解 by institutionalizing plurality as pedagogy. It differs from Chu’s Zhuangzi sea by being a fixed tetrad of authorities rather than an open anthology—why its method is stratified curriculum, not research archive."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "洞靈真經註",
      "logic_thesis": "Commentary on the Dongling (Wenzi/Gengsangzi) corpus proves that Huang-Lao governance and inner quiet share one logic: the sage empties private will so that response can match the pattern of things. Political non-coercion and personal non-disturbance are the same proof written at two scales.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Forcing order against the grain multiplies disorder in body and state.
Premise 2: Soft alignment with Dao (stillness, timing, frugality of action) restores function.
Inference 1: Therefore self-cultivation is the micro-model of rule, and rule is the macro-test of cultivation.
Inference 2: Textual instruction that links virtue, emptiness, and timing is practical science, not dual track.
Conclusion: Dongling learning proves continuity between quiet mind and effective, light-touch action in the world.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Apply “less forcing” as a measurable rule: reduce interventions that create secondary problems.
2. Time actions to seasonal and chart weather rather than to anxiety urgency.
3. Govern speech and household as a miniature polity: fewer laws, clearer examples.
4. Use stillness sessions to improve decision quality, then re-enter affairs.
5. Score cultivation by reduced coercion needed to keep life workable.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike pure Sanhuang ritual texts, it argues from principle of soft governance, not register magic. Unlike 無能子, which radicalizes equality against rulers, Dongling commentary still assumes ordered roles—why its emptiness serves refined rule rather than abolishing hierarchy."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "無能子",
      "logic_thesis": "Wunengzi proves that hierarchical prestige, ritual stiffening, and monarchical compulsion are historical deviations from natural human equality and quiet life-force. If nature is the standard, then “greatness” that multiplies desire and rank is a disease; true ability is the ability to remain without artificial power.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Humans originally share qi and basic needs without fixed masters.
Premise 2: Names, rites, and thrones intensify comparison and violence.
Inference 1: Therefore critique of authority is not politics alone but recovery of natural reason.
Inference 2: Cultivation (sitting-forgetting, less desire) and social equality reinforce each other.
Conclusion: The text proves that spiritual freedom requires dismantling false “ability,” including the ability to dominate.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Audit BaZi ambition language: which goals are rank-addiction wearing destiny’s mask?
2. Practice anonymity drills: do good without identity yield.
3. Reduce status signaling in learning (titles, secretism) that recreates hierarchy inside Dao.
4. Prefer equalizing care (shared benefit) over techniques that empower one against many.
5. Use “no-ability” as a check: if a method increases craving for superiority, drop it.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from Jingming’s 四規, which sanctifies loyalty-filiality as Dao’s root, by treating much social virtue-talk as potential cover for domination. It differs from Wang Pang’s Zhuangzi, which saves public order, by pushing naturalness toward anti-authoritarian critique—why Tang crisis energy is audible in its logic."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "玄真子外篇",
      "logic_thesis": "Zhang Zhihe proves that the cosmos is a creative performance of transformation—more drum-and-pipe of change than a moral courtroom—so the sage’s task is to join the music rather than prosecute it. Knowing “the utmost Dao has no thing” liberates perception into playful participation without ownerly control.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Transformations of beings are continuous and not owned by any final substance.
Premise 2: Conceptual grasping freezes the music into dead objects.
Inference 1: Therefore discourse should mimic metamorphosis (parable, irony, shifting speakers).
Inference 2: The mind that can face transformation without panic becomes “true and darkly complete.”
Conclusion: Outer chapters prove spiritual success as aesthetic-ontological attunement, not as conquest of fate.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Treat luck cycles as key changes in a piece of music: enter the key, don’t fight the modulation.
2. Practice perceptual play: rename a problem three ways to loosen fixation.
3. Create without clutching outcomes (art, craft, experiment) as training for non-ownership.
4. In BaZi, emphasize transformation gods and phase shifts over static good/bad stamps.
5. End sessions by releasing the interpreter-self that wants to “finish” the cosmos.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 素履子, which proves through sober ethical walking, 玄真子 proves through imaginative cosmology. Unlike 心目論, which stages a moral trial between heart and eyes, Zhang’s logic is less forensic and more polyphonic—why the cure is participation, not only restraint."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "素履子",
      "logic_thesis": "Zhang Hu’s Suluizi proves that the Dao is verified in plain, consistent conduct—walking in plain shoes—rather than in display of mystery. Integrity of daily steps is the argument: without simple virtue, metaphysical talk is counterfeit currency.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: People seek rare techniques while neglecting ordinary faithfulness.
Premise 2: The Dao of heaven is near in measured, sincere action.
Inference 1: Therefore teaching must return to duties, frugality, and steady mind.
Inference 2: When conduct is plain and aligned, fortune and clarity follow as side effects.
Conclusion: “Plain walking” is the proof-procedure of Daoist life against theatrical esotericism.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Convert one chart weakness into a daily micro-habit (sleep, speech honesty, spending) for 40 days.
2. Prefer boring consistency over intense weekend cultivation spikes.
3. Before advanced methods, pass a conduct audit: lies, excess, broken promises.
4. Use BaZi annual advice only if it can be stated as a plain behavioral rule.
5. Measure the year by fewer self-betrayals, not by rarer omens.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from 玄真子’s cosmic play by insisting on ethical footwork. It differs from Jingming’s 四規 by being general Tang moral-Dao discourse rather than a sectarian system of loyalty-filial “gates”—why its logic is pedestrian in the best sense: truth must be walkable."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "心目論",
      "logic_thesis": "Wu Yun proves that spiritual ruin is primarily perceptual: the eyes drag the heart into restlessness, so the heart cannot abide in non-action. By staging a debate between heart and eyes, the text shows that mastery of attention is the root method; without it, all higher Dao is noise.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Spirit lives in the heart-mind; form is its lodging.
Premise 2: The eyes continuously import objects that agitate the heart.
Inference 1: An agitated heart exhausts spirit and collapses the body.
Inference 2: Therefore one must restrain the gates of seeing (and cognate senses) to restore stillness.
Conclusion: Quietude is not abstract metaphysics but the victory of the heart’s non-action over the eyes’ compulsion.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Install eye-fasts: fixed hours without scrolling, novelty, or lustful looking.
2. When chart anxiety spikes, locate the sensory trigger first, then the story.
3. Practice “heart as host”: let seeing occur without the heart chasing.
4. Use short sittings focused only on withdrawing attention from the visual stream.
5. Track cultivation by reduced reactivity to images, not by accumulated concepts.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike 太平經聖君秘旨, which centers the metaphysical One and luminous vision as fruit, 心目論 treats vision mainly as the problem to be tamed. Unlike 中黄八柱经, which systematizes many orifices and pillars, Wu Yun isolates one decisive conflict—heart versus eyes—as the master switch."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "太平經聖君秘旨",
      "logic_thesis": "This digest proves that longevity and social peace share one technique: guard the One so that essence, qi, and spirit reunite. Multiplicity of knowledge without the One scatters life; concentrated shouyi generates inner light, repels harm, and radiates order outward without forceful labor.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Essence, qi, and spirit are one root split into three cooperative functions.
Premise 2: Longevity fails when the three separate; disasters multiply when nothing is held as One.
Inference 1: Guarding the formless origin reunites the three and births inner brightness.
Inference 2: Inner brightness becomes outer order (body, household, realm) by resonance, not strain.
Conclusion: Shouyi is the master key: know the One and the ten thousand affairs complete themselves.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Daily shouyi block: sit, reduce knowing, hold formless unity for a timed period.
2. In BaZi terms, locate the chart’s “One” (day-master balance point or useful coherence) and stop chasing every god.
3. Practice three-treasures hygiene: sleep/sexual conservation (essence), breath (qi), calm focus (spirit).
4. Use progressive duration (weeks) as the text’s arithmetic of benefit, not one-off intensity.
5. Let outer reforms follow only after inner unity is stable.",
      "logic_compare": "Unlike Sanhuang zhai texts, proof here is interior concentration rather than register petition. Unlike Jingming ethics, it does not begin with loyalty-filial codes; it begins with ontological One—why its politics of “Great Peace” is framed as a physiological-spiritual resonance of shouyi."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "太上靈寶首入淨明四規明鑑經",
      "logic_thesis": "This Jingming entry text proves that Dao is not imported from outside but fulfilled by extending innate filial-brotherly nature into loyalty and completed deeds. Without the four regulations as a mirror, techniques and quiet sitting become self-deception; ethical luminosity is the gate of immortality.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Dao belongs to nature; filiality and brotherliness are not forced add-ons.
Premise 2: Extending that nature into loyalty and public benefit ripens conduct.
Inference 1: Conduct completeness daily fills the Dao; skipping ethics hollows practice.
Inference 2: The four mirrors diagnose failures at root, body-cultivation, merit, and completion.
Conclusion: Net-brightness (jingming) is moral clarity that simultaneously purifies heart and authorizes higher attainment.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Begin each BaZi/year plan with a loyalty-filial audit of actual relationships, not abstract ideals.
2. Translate “merit” into concrete service that reduces others’ hardship.
3. Use the four chapters as a checklist: root motive, self-cultivation, deeds, good ending.
4. Reject secret methods while family and civic duties are in open breach.
5. Define success as unobscured conscience plus stable life, not only power experiences.",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from 中黄八柱经 by prioritizing social-ethical gates before somatic architecture. It differs from 無能子 by sacralizing hierarchical virtues (zhong, xiao) as Dao’s root rather than suspecting them—why Jingming could integrate Confucian order into immortal striving."
    },
    {
      "name_han": "太上靈寶淨明中黃八柱經",
      "logic_thesis": "This text proves that correct position (center, yellow) is the precondition of all higher work: empty the four sensory valleys, seal the two leakage gates, open the two fluid-spirit caverns, and the eight pillars of the body-house stand. Immortality technique is architectural integrity of the person, not scattered tricks.",
      "logic_chain": "Premise 1: Life is received as balanced pure qi; disease is loss of center.
Premise 2: Eyes, ears, mouth, nose and the two leakage portals either protect or destroy that center.
Inference 1: Emptying false inputs and sealing leaks conserves essence-qi for the middle.
Inference 2: Opening crown and palate pathways then allows circulation and “golden elixir” function.
Conclusion: Establish center and eight pillars first; only then can nature be true and the path long.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Daily: reduce non-seeing/hearing/tasting/smelling noise (empty four valleys).
2. Seal leaks: regulate lust and idle expenditure of qi (speech, anger, overeating).
3. Gentle “open caverns”: upright posture, soft breathing, clear swallow/saliva practice without strain.
4. In BaZi, treat the useful center (balance of day-master) as “zhonghuang”; strengthen it before chasing peripheral gods.
5. Build life like a house: foundation (yuanqi), pillars (restraints and openings), then decoration (advanced rites).",
      "logic_compare": "It differs from 四規明鑑經 by moving from civic-ethical entry to precise somatic engineering. It differs from 思印气诀法 by turning the same mind-qi discipline inward as permanent architecture rather than outward as a stamp of command."

Premise 2: Techniques of self-preservation can yield long life without opening the great vehicle of salvation.
Inference 1: Therefore envy of higher beings is misdiagnosed; the missing variable is causal merit.
Inference 2: Re-set intention toward rescuing beings and practicing Lingbao methods to rewrite future rank.
Conclusion: Destiny is plastic through cause-and-vow education, not through lifespan-stacking alone.",
      "logic_practice": "1. Read BaZi “rank” and “longevity” separately: long life ≠ high spiritual station.
2. Inventory vows actually lived (whom you save, whom you ignore) as the real causal chart.

entries.name_han: 太上三皇宝斋神仙上录经
entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that immortality is not a private mental achievement but a juridical-liturgical status granted when pure zhai, correct offerings, and the Sanhuang register cohere. Personal refinement alone is insufficient; only sustained abstinence, lamp-smoke, and petition that clear seven-generation debt can rewrite the celestial ledger and admit the adept to the immortal roster.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Three Sovereigns hold the prenatal register that names life, death, and rank.
Premise 2: Multigenerational sin and impurity block the register from opening to the living.
Inference 1: Therefore only rigorous zhai (silence, timed meals, pure water, incense) can sever contamination and make petition audible.
Inference 2: When lamps and fragrant beads transmit intent, heavenly officers reverse black-book entries and fix the immortal name.
Conclusion: Long life and spirit-summoning power are consequences of register correction, not of technique without liturgy.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Treat chart-clearing as zhai before reading BaZi: fix intention, reduce sensory noise, then open the pillars.
2. Sequence work as debt → purity → petition: first name ancestral and personal blockages, then refine qi, then act.
3. Use timed “lamp” discipline (fixed watches of quiet focus) to mark when intention is clean enough to decide.
4. Do not attempt spirit-calling or fate-override operations until three sustained cycles of purity have held.
5. Measure success by lighter body-mind and freer timing, not by dramatic visions.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 三皇内秘文, which argues from cosmogony and seal-command, this text argues from ritual procedure and register law. Unlike later Jingming ethics texts, it does not moralize social virtue first; it moralizes purity and petition as the only legitimate path into the Sanhuang bureaucracy.

entries.name_han: 太清金阙玉华仙书八极神章三皇内秘文
entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that all spirits, disasters, and remedies are effects of one generative process: True-One → yuanqi → differentiation into heaven, earth, humans, gods, and deviant classes. Command over ghosts and disease is therefore legitimate only when the operator re-aligns with that same True-One hierarchy, not when he merely stacks stronger spells.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Before images, True-One already moves; yuanqi self-transforms into clear, turbid, harmonious, and deviant forms.
Premise 2: Eight Extremes, Five Peaks, and ghost-types are handles of that one body of qi, not rival cosmologies.
Inference 1: Evil is misaligned residue of the same root, so it answers to names and seals that restore order.
Inference 2: Therefore talisman and summoning work only when the operator’s moral-cosmic station matches the chapter’s hierarchy.
Conclusion: Mastery of the Sanhuang secret chapters is re-participation in cosmogony, which then authorizes exorcism and protection.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Map BaZi ten gods and six relations onto “classes of qi” (supportive, deviant, pure, turbid) rather than as mere labels.
2. Before remedial rituals, state the root principle (True-One / yuanqi) so technique is not freestanding magic.
3. Rank remedies: first correct self-station and timing, then address external “ghost” or disaster patterns.
4. Use directional/Eight Extremes thinking for spatial luck: treat place as a handle of the same qi body.
5. Reject techniques that claim power without re-centering the operator in the generative hierarchy.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 思印气诀法 by supplying ontology before method; seals here are secondary to cosmology. It differs from pure Zhuangzi commentaries by treating hierarchy and command as real, not as illusions to dissolve—why the text can authorize active demonology rather than only contemplative freedom.

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that a seal’s efficacy is not material inscription alone but the temporary identity of mind-image, directed qi, and ritual seal. When tooth-clicking, mudra, paced steps, inhaled qi, and visualization fuse, the seal becomes a portable center of command that can bind landscape, illness, and disorder.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Spirits and places respond to concentrated intention embodied as form.
Premise 2: Qi follows breath and attention; seals store and project that form.
Inference 1: Therefore the operator must first assemble inner court (teeth, mudra, Yu steps, color-coded officers).
Inference 2: Blowing qi into the seal charges the form; stamping or sealing then transfers that charge to a target domain.
Conclusion: Control of mountains, seas, epidemics, or thieves is the extension of a completed mind-qi-seal circuit, not of ink alone.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Before any BaZi remedy or space-clearing, complete a short assembly: settle breath, set intention, form a clear “seal” image of the desired order.
2. Use paced movement and timed exhalation to move qi into a concrete symbol (hand, talisman, or written name).
3. Apply the charged form only to one domain at a time (room, body, conflict) to avoid diffuse intention.
4. After stamping/sealing, withdraw qi and store the form; do not leave residual excitement.
5. Test efficacy by environmental shift (calmer place, fewer disruptions), not by emotional hype.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 三皇宝斋, which proves through multi-day zhai and celestial ledger, this text proves through a compact operational circuit. Unlike 中黄八柱经, which builds an internal architecture of virtue and orifices, 思印气诀法 externalizes the same mind-qi unity into a tool that acts on the outer world.

entries.logic_thesis: Cheng Xuanying’s double-mystery (chongxuan) reading proves that liberation is the successive emptying of both attachment and attachment-to-emptiness. Guo Xiang’s “each thing is self-so” is not final; the adept must also forget the very stance of self-so, so that neither being nor non-being remains as a grip.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Fixed is/ought dualisms generate suffering and false mastery.
Premise 2: Guo Xiang dissolves artificial standards into natural allotment (ziran, duxua).
Inference 1: Yet holding “allotment” as doctrine reinstalls a subtle self.
Inference 2: Therefore one must negate both affirmation and negation (twofold mystery).
Conclusion: True free-and-easy wandering is not settling into nature as an idea, but the unobstructed functioning after both poles drop.
entries.logic_practice:
1. When a BaZi pattern feels fatal, first drop moral panic, then drop the pride of “accepting fate.”
2. Practice two-step release: name the attachment, then name the attachment to being free of it.
3. Use chart reading as diagnosis of current conditions, not as an identity the self must defend.
4. In meditation, alternate “rest in what is” with “do not rest even in resting” for short cycles.
5. Measure progress by reduced need to win interpretive fights about destiny.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from Wang Pang’s 新傳, which retools Zhuangzi for political-moral usefulness, by treating usefulness itself as a trap to empty. It differs from Lin Xiyi’s 口義, which clarifies plain sense for readers, by pushing beyond sense into a method of successive apophasis.

entries.logic_thesis: Wang Pang proves that Zhuangzi’s free wandering is not social withdrawal but the inner basis of correct public order: only a mind that has loosened private compulsion can respond to affairs without distortion. The text argues that Daoist freedom and Confucian responsibility are one continuum when the heart is no longer hijacked by fixed names.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Political and personal disorder arise from stiff names and private desire.
Premise 2: Zhuangzi’s transformation and equalization loosen those grips.
Inference 1: A loosened mind can then take up roles without being owned by them.
Inference 2: Therefore commentary must translate parable into principles of self-governance and statecraft.
Conclusion: The “new transmission” is Zhuangzi re-proved as practical wisdom for ordering self and realm, not as aesthetic escapism.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Read day/luck pillars as roles you inhabit, not as essences you are.
2. Before major decisions, ask: is this response from loosened awareness or from a name I am defending?
3. Train “useful uselessness”: keep capacity without forcing every hour into achievement.
4. In conflict charts, equalize viewpoints first, then choose the action that least reinstalls compulsion.
5. Use cultivation to improve public-facing clarity (speech, timing), not only private calm.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Cheng Xuanying’s double mystery, which empties both poles, Wang Pang stops at a usable equilibrium that serves ethics and politics. Unlike 無能子, which weaponizes naturalness against hierarchy, 新傳 rehabilitated hierarchy by purifying the mind that must still act within it.

entries.logic_thesis: Lin Xiyi proves that Zhuangzi’s difficulty is largely pedagogical: when parable, humor, and “absurd” images are restored to spoken sense, the argument about transforming life becomes teachable without esoteric monopoly. Clarity of ordinary language is itself a method of equalizing access to the Dao.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Obscure classical glosses recreate the very scholastic ego Zhuangzi mocks.
Premise 2: Oral paraphrase recovers narrative intent and human situation.
Inference 1: Therefore correct understanding is tested by whether a listener can apply it today.
Inference 2: Application without jargon dissolves false profundity.
Conclusion: “Mouth-meaning” is not vulgarization but a proof that the Dao operates in plain life when speech stops performing status.
entries.logic_practice:
1. After any BaZi analysis, restate the whole chart in one plain sentence a non-specialist could use.
2. Drop ornamental jargon in cultivation notes; keep only verbs of practice.
3. Teach transformation with stories of daily pressure (work, family), not only with classical tags.
4. Use humor and self-undercutting to break reading-as-status.
5. Verify insight by behavioral change within one week, not by elegant formulation.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 義海纂微 by refusing encyclopedic plurality in favor of one lucid reading path. It differs from 循本, which seeks philological “original intent,” by prioritizing living intelligibility over archaeological purity—why Lin’s text became a gateway rather than a scholarly fortress.

entries.logic_thesis: Chu Boxiu proves that no single commentator owns Zhuangzi; truth emerges by setting many lineages side by side until shared structure and productive differences appear. Anthology is an epistemic method: the “sea of meanings” disciplines both sectarian capture and private whim.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Guo, Cheng, Song Confucians, and Daoist readers each catch partial angles.
Premise 2: Isolated reading mistakes a partial angle for the whole.
Inference 1: Collecting and arranging them reveals recurring logic (equalization, transformation, free wandering).
Inference 2: Divergence then becomes diagnostic of method, not merely error.
Conclusion: Understanding is a comparative operation across a tradition, not submission to one master voice.
entries.logic_practice:
1. For hard BaZi questions, deliberately consult three incompatible models, then extract only the overlapping constraints.
2. Keep a comparative notebook: same passage / chart feature, multiple readings, one residual certainty.
3. Treat disagreement as information about method bias (moral, empty, political, philological).
4. Refuse early closure when only one school flatters your preference.
5. Synthesize practice rules only after patterns recur across sources.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 口義’s single plain path, 義海纂微 multiplies paths to prevent monopoly. Unlike 循本, which rejects Chan-tinged and freestyle notes to recover “the root,” Chu’s work preserves the archive so that “the root” can be checked against history rather than asserted.

entries.logic_thesis: Chen Jingyuan proves that sound, graph, and chapter division are not pedantry but the first filters of thought: wrong pronunciation and false segmentation generate metaphysical ghosts. Philology is thus a spiritual hygiene that returns the text’s movement before doctrine is built.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Meaning rides on correct wording, rhythm, and unit of argument.
Premise 2: Later metaphysics often rests on corrupt or forced readings.
Inference 1: Therefore chapter-and-sentence work and sound-meaning notes must precede lofty claims.
Inference 2: Where Yijing and correlative patterns genuinely help structure, they must still answer to the restored text.
Conclusion: Authentic free wandering begins with textual fidelity that prevents self-projected Dao.
entries.logic_practice:
1. In BaZi, define every technical term before interpreting (what “cai” means operationally this month).
2. Re-segment life narratives: wrong “chapter breaks” create false destiny stories.
3. Prefer small, text-true rules over grand symbolic systems that ignore data.
4. When using Five-Phase or Yijing overlays, demand a textual or observational warrant.
5. Audit your own notes for words that sound deep but do no diagnostic work.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from Cheng’s mystical double-emptying by starting below metaphysics, at the letter. It differs from Wang Pang’s moral-political rewrite by refusing to skip the text’s grain; Chen’s “why” is that corrupt sound-sense is already a form of self-assertion.

entries.logic_thesis: Luo Miandao proves that later Zhuangzi industries—pure talk, forced Yijing, and Chan overlays—lose the book’s own spine (for him, often “transformation” as continuous thread). Returning to the root is a critical method: cut secondary cleverness until the text’s native argument reappears.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Commentarial fashion multiplies meanings that serve schools, not Zhuangzi.
Premise 2: A text has internal recurrence and narrative logic that can discipline reading.
Inference 1: Tracking that internal thread (“follow the root”) exposes alien grafts.
Inference 2: What cannot be justified by the text’s own movement is set aside.
Conclusion: Liberation teaching must be reclaimed from hybrid display and restored to Zhuangzi’s self-consistent path.
entries.logic_practice:
1. For any cultivation claim, ask: what single thread in my practice does this serve? Drop ornaments.
2. In chart work, pick one structural key (e.g., useful god, day-master balance) and follow it end-to-end.
3. Reject methods that only add prestige metaphors without changing decisions.
4. Periodically return to primary experiences (breath, timing, consequence) to reset theory.
5. Prefer fewer consistent rules over a collage of impressive schools.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 義海纂微’s generous archive, 循本 is exclusionary by design: plurality is the disease. Unlike 口義’s accessibility project, Luo’s project is authenticity policing—why his “why” is anti-syncretic where Lin’s is anti-elitist.

entries.logic_thesis: Jiang Yu’s Liezi commentary proves that stories of dreams, skill, fate, and the infinite are engines for releasing the will’s claim to mastery. Reading Liezi correctly means converting marvel into a discipline of yielding: destiny is not denied, but the anxious self that fights destiny is dissolved.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Liezi multiplies limit-cases (dream/waking, finite/infinite, effort/fate).
Premise 2: These cases break ordinary agency without preaching nihilism.
Inference 1: Commentary must show how each tale loosens a specific grip (control, fame, cleverness).
Inference 2: The freed person then acts with skill like the butcher or boatman—without forcing.
Conclusion: Chongxu (“pouring emptiness”) is proven as practical non-resistance that still allows exquisite function.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Use hard luck periods as dream/waking training: notice which “self” is panicking.
2. Practice skill-without-forcing in one craft (speech, writing, body work) as Liezi’s craftsmen do.
3. When BaZi shows constraint, shift from “how do I overturn” to “where is non-resistance intelligent.”
4. Alternate contemplation of vast scale (time, heaven) with next small action.
5. Drop debates that only restore the will’s sense of control.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Zhuangzi’s more rhetorical equalization, Liezi (as Jiang reads it) often proves through narrative shock and fatalism-tempered skill. Unlike 四解, which layers four authorities, this single-author 解 seeks a unified Guo-like philosophical voice rather than a chorus.

entries.logic_thesis: The four-layer Liezi (Zhang Zhan, Lu Chongxuan, Huizong, Fan Zhixu) proves that the same parable supports successive altitudes of reading—from metaphysical emptiness to cultivated practice to imperial instruction—without collapsing into one slogan. Multi-commentary is a ladder: each rung answers a different failure mode of the reader.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: A single gloss cannot serve novices, adepts, and rulers equally.
Premise 2: Liezi’s tales are polyvalent by design.
Inference 1: Stacking historically distinct exegeses exposes complementary functions of one story.
Inference 2: The reader learns to choose the layer that corrects their present disease (doubt, rigidity, ambition, despair).
Conclusion: “Four explanations” demonstrate that truth is one process of emptying and trusting process, taught through calibrated voices.
entries.logic_practice:
1. For one life problem, write four responses: empty view, practice view, ethical view, strategic view; keep only what reduces friction.
2. Use Zhang-style ontology when anxious about meaning; use practice layers when lazy or diffuse.
3. In BaZi teaching, match explanation depth to the querent’s actual bottleneck.
4. Do not force imperial/political readings onto private grief, or private quietism onto public duty.
5. Revisit the same classic seasonally; different layers will “light up.”
entries.logic_compare: It differs from Jiang Yu’s single philosophical 解 by institutionalizing plurality as pedagogy. It differs from Chu’s Zhuangzi sea by being a fixed tetrad of authorities rather than an open anthology—why its method is stratified curriculum, not research archive.

entries.logic_thesis: Commentary on the Dongling (Wenzi/Gengsangzi) corpus proves that Huang-Lao governance and inner quiet share one logic: the sage empties private will so that response can match the pattern of things. Political non-coercion and personal non-disturbance are the same proof written at two scales.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Forcing order against the grain multiplies disorder in body and state.
Premise 2: Soft alignment with Dao (stillness, timing, frugality of action) restores function.
Inference 1: Therefore self-cultivation is the micro-model of rule, and rule is the macro-test of cultivation.
Inference 2: Textual instruction that links virtue, emptiness, and timing is practical science, not dual track.
Conclusion: Dongling learning proves continuity between quiet mind and effective, light-touch action in the world.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Apply “less forcing” as a measurable rule: reduce interventions that create secondary problems.
2. Time actions to seasonal and chart weather rather than to anxiety urgency.
3. Govern speech and household as a miniature polity: fewer laws, clearer examples.
4. Use stillness sessions to improve decision quality, then re-enter affairs.
5. Score cultivation by reduced coercion needed to keep life workable.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure Sanhuang ritual texts, it argues from principle of soft governance, not register magic. Unlike 無能子, which radicalizes equality against rulers, Dongling commentary still assumes ordered roles—why its emptiness serves refined rule rather than abolishing hierarchy.

entries.logic_thesis: Wunengzi proves that hierarchical prestige, ritual stiffening, and monarchical compulsion are historical deviations from natural human equality and quiet life-force. If nature is the standard, then “greatness” that multiplies desire and rank is a disease; true ability is the ability to remain without artificial power.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Humans originally share qi and basic needs without fixed masters.
Premise 2: Names, rites, and thrones intensify comparison and violence.
Inference 1: Therefore critique of authority is not politics alone but recovery of natural reason.
Inference 2: Cultivation (sitting-forgetting, less desire) and social equality reinforce each other.
Conclusion: The text proves that spiritual freedom requires dismantling false “ability,” including the ability to dominate.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Audit BaZi ambition language: which goals are rank-addiction wearing destiny’s mask?
2. Practice anonymity drills: do good without identity yield.
3. Reduce status signaling in learning (titles, secretism) that recreates hierarchy inside Dao.
4. Prefer equalizing care (shared benefit) over techniques that empower one against many.
5. Use “no-ability” as a check: if a method increases craving for superiority, drop it.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from Jingming’s 四規, which sanctifies loyalty-filiality as Dao’s root, by treating much social virtue-talk as potential cover for domination. It differs from Wang Pang’s Zhuangzi, which saves public order, by pushing naturalness toward anti-authoritarian critique—why Tang crisis energy is audible in its logic.

entries.logic_thesis: Zhang Zhihe proves that the cosmos is a creative performance of transformation—more drum-and-pipe of change than a moral courtroom—so the sage’s task is to join the music rather than prosecute it. Knowing “the utmost Dao has no thing” liberates perception into playful participation without ownerly control.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Transformations of beings are continuous and not owned by any final substance.
Premise 2: Conceptual grasping freezes the music into dead objects.
Inference 1: Therefore discourse should mimic metamorphosis (parable, irony, shifting speakers).
Inference 2: The mind that can face transformation without panic becomes “true and darkly complete.”
Conclusion: Outer chapters prove spiritual success as aesthetic-ontological attunement, not as conquest of fate.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Treat luck cycles as key changes in a piece of music: enter the key, don’t fight the modulation.
2. Practice perceptual play: rename a problem three ways to loosen fixation.
3. Create without clutching outcomes (art, craft, experiment) as training for non-ownership.
4. In BaZi, emphasize transformation gods and phase shifts over static good/bad stamps.
5. End sessions by releasing the interpreter-self that wants to “finish” the cosmos.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 素履子, which proves through sober ethical walking, 玄真子 proves through imaginative cosmology. Unlike 心目論, which stages a moral trial between heart and eyes, Zhang’s logic is less forensic and more polyphonic—why the cure is participation, not only restraint.

entries.logic_thesis: Zhang Hu’s Suluizi proves that the Dao is verified in plain, consistent conduct—walking in plain shoes—rather than in display of mystery. Integrity of daily steps is the argument: without simple virtue, metaphysical talk is counterfeit currency.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: People seek rare techniques while neglecting ordinary faithfulness.
Premise 2: The Dao of heaven is near in measured, sincere action.
Inference 1: Therefore teaching must return to duties, frugality, and steady mind.
Inference 2: When conduct is plain and aligned, fortune and clarity follow as side effects.
Conclusion: “Plain walking” is the proof-procedure of Daoist life against theatrical esotericism.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Convert one chart weakness into a daily micro-habit (sleep, speech honesty, spending) for 40 days.
2. Prefer boring consistency over intense weekend cultivation spikes.
3. Before advanced methods, pass a conduct audit: lies, excess, broken promises.
4. Use BaZi annual advice only if it can be stated as a plain behavioral rule.
5. Measure the year by fewer self-betrayals, not by rarer omens.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 玄真子’s cosmic play by insisting on ethical footwork. It differs from Jingming’s 四規 by being general Tang moral-Dao discourse rather than a sectarian system of loyalty-filial “gates”—why its logic is pedestrian in the best sense: truth must be walkable.

entries.logic_thesis: Wu Yun proves that spiritual ruin is primarily perceptual: the eyes drag the heart into restlessness, so the heart cannot abide in non-action. By staging a debate between heart and eyes, the text shows that mastery of attention is the root method; without it, all higher Dao is noise.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Spirit lives in the heart-mind; form is its lodging.
Premise 2: The eyes continuously import objects that agitate the heart.
Inference 1: An agitated heart exhausts spirit and collapses the body.
Inference 2: Therefore one must restrain the gates of seeing (and cognate senses) to restore stillness.
Conclusion: Quietude is not abstract metaphysics but the victory of the heart’s non-action over the eyes’ compulsion.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Install eye-fasts: fixed hours without scrolling, novelty, or lustful looking.
2. When chart anxiety spikes, locate the sensory trigger first, then the story.
3. Practice “heart as host”: let seeing occur without the heart chasing.
4. Use short sittings focused only on withdrawing attention from the visual stream.
5. Track cultivation by reduced reactivity to images, not by accumulated concepts.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 太平經聖君秘旨, which centers the metaphysical One and luminous vision as fruit, 心目論 treats vision mainly as the problem to be tamed. Unlike 中黄八柱经, which systematizes many orifices and pillars, Wu Yun isolates one decisive conflict—heart versus eyes—as the master switch.

entries.logic_thesis: This digest proves that longevity and social peace share one technique: guard the One so that essence, qi, and spirit reunite. Multiplicity of knowledge without the One scatters life; concentrated shouyi generates inner light, repels harm, and radiates order outward without forceful labor.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Essence, qi, and spirit are one root split into three cooperative functions.
Premise 2: Longevity fails when the three separate; disasters multiply when nothing is held as One.
Inference 1: Guarding the formless origin reunites the three and births inner brightness.
Inference 2: Inner brightness becomes outer order (body, household, realm) by resonance, not strain.
Conclusion: Shouyi is the master key: know the One and the ten thousand affairs complete themselves.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Daily shouyi block: sit, reduce knowing, hold formless unity for a timed period.
2. In BaZi terms, locate the chart’s “One” (day-master balance point or useful coherence) and stop chasing every god.
3. Practice three-treasures hygiene: sleep/sexual conservation (essence), breath (qi), calm focus (spirit).
4. Use progressive duration (weeks) as the text’s arithmetic of benefit, not one-off intensity.
5. Let outer reforms follow only after inner unity is stable.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Sanhuang zhai texts, proof here is interior concentration rather than register petition. Unlike Jingming ethics, it does not begin with loyalty-filial codes; it begins with ontological One—why its politics of “Great Peace” is framed as a physiological-spiritual resonance of shouyi.

entries.name_han: 太上靈寶首入淨明四規明鑑經
entries.logic_thesis: This Jingming entry text proves that Dao is not imported from outside but fulfilled by extending innate filial-brotherly nature into loyalty and completed deeds. Without the four regulations as a mirror, techniques and quiet sitting become self-deception; ethical luminosity is the gate of immortality.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Dao belongs to nature; filiality and brotherliness are not forced add-ons.
Premise 2: Extending that nature into loyalty and public benefit ripens conduct.
Inference 1: Conduct completeness daily fills the Dao; skipping ethics hollows practice.
Inference 2: The four mirrors diagnose failures at root, body-cultivation, merit, and completion.
Conclusion: Net-brightness (jingming) is moral clarity that simultaneously purifies heart and authorizes higher attainment.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Begin each BaZi/year plan with a loyalty-filial audit of actual relationships, not abstract ideals.
2. Translate “merit” into concrete service that reduces others’ hardship.
3. Use the four chapters as a checklist: root motive, self-cultivation, deeds, good ending.
4. Reject secret methods while family and civic duties are in open breach.
5. Define success as unobscured conscience plus stable life, not only power experiences.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 中黄八柱经 by prioritizing social-ethical gates before somatic architecture. It differs from 無能子 by sacralizing hierarchical virtues (zhong, xiao) as Dao’s root rather than suspecting them—why Jingming could integrate Confucian order into immortal striving.

entries.name_han: 太上靈寶淨明中黃八柱經
entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that correct position (center, yellow) is the precondition of all higher work: empty the four sensory valleys, seal the two leakage gates, open the two fluid-spirit caverns, and the eight pillars of the body-house stand. Immortality technique is architectural integrity of the person, not scattered tricks.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Life is received as balanced pure qi; disease is loss of center.
Premise 2: Eyes, ears, mouth, nose and the two leakage portals either protect or destroy that center.
Inference 1: Emptying false inputs and sealing leaks conserves essence-qi for the middle.
Inference 2: Opening crown and palate pathways then allows circulation and “golden elixir” function.
Conclusion: Establish center and eight pillars first; only then can nature be true and the path long.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Daily: reduce non-seeing/hearing/tasting/smelling noise (empty four valleys).
2. Seal leaks: regulate lust and idle expenditure of qi (speech, anger, overeating).
3. Gentle “open caverns”: upright posture, soft breathing, clear swallow/saliva practice without strain.
4. In BaZi, treat the useful center (balance of day-master) as “zhonghuang”; strengthen it before chasing peripheral gods.
5. Build life like a house: foundation (yuanqi), pillars (restraints and openings), then decoration (advanced rites).
entries.logic_compare: It differs from 四規明鑑經 by moving from civic-ethical entry to precise somatic engineering. It differs from 思印气诀法 by turning the same mind-qi discipline inward as permanent architecture rather than outward as a stamp of command.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄靈寶本行因緣經
entries.logic_thesis: Through Ge Xuan’s exchange with earth immortals, this Lingbao scripture proves that rank in the immortal hierarchy tracks the quality of original vows and saving deeds, not mere longevity techniques. Long life without universal merit remains a lesser causal fruit; higher ascent requires re-planting causes in compassionate action and scriptural practice.
entries.logic_chain:
Premise 1: Present station (earth immortal vs higher) is the fruit of past vows and deeds.
Premise 2: Techniques of self-preservation can yield long life without opening the great vehicle of salvation.
Inference 1: Therefore envy of higher beings is misdiagnosed; the missing variable is causal merit.
Inference 2: Re-set intention toward rescuing beings and practicing Lingbao methods to rewrite future rank.
Conclusion: Destiny is plastic through cause-and-vow education, not through lifespan-stacking alone.
entries.logic_practice:
1. Read BaZi “rank” and “longevity” separately: long life ≠ high spiritual station.
2. Inventory vows actually lived (whom you save, whom you ignore) as the real causal chart.
3. Add periodic merit practice (teaching, aid, ritual for others) as deliberately planted causes.
4. When stuck in a plateau, change the vow-structure rather than only the technique stack.
5. Evaluate progress by increased capacity to benefit others under the same constraints.
entries.logic_compare: It differs from Sanhuang zhai register logic by emphasizing Mahayana-style universal salvation vows rather than primarily personal ledger clearing. It differs from Jingming’s present-life loyalty-filial focus by foregrounding multi-life causal narrative and graded immortal bureaucracy—why its proof is karmic pedagogy rather than only ethical mirror or somatic house-building.
